data.long_meaning: In Greek mythology, Artemis is the goddess of the hunt, wilderness, wild animals, the Moon, and chastity. Daughter of Leto and Zeus, she is the twin sister of Apollo. The name Artemisa carries the meaning “Goddess of the hunt” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Artemisa usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the hunt and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Artemisa total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

data.cultural_impact: Artemis was believed to protect women in childbirth and aid them during labor. She was also known for her abilities in healing and her role as the goddess of the hunt. The worship of Artemis spread throughout the ancient Greek world, and numerous temples were built in her honor. She was revered in both public and private cults, and her festivals were an important part of Greek life.
data.spiritual_significance: Artemis represents the untamed and fierce aspects of nature. She is the protector of wild animals and the wilderness, and she embodies the power and independence of women. Her association with the moon underscores her connection to the cycles of nature and the rhythms of life. In Christianity, the name Artemis may be seen as a reminder of the rich cultural and spiritual heritage that preceded the emergence of the Christian faith. It may also be seen as a symbol of the strength and resilience of the natural world and the divine feminine.
